memberAssessments.reason: Jin053s0002 explicitly identifies 湣懷太子遹，字熙祖，惠帝長子，母曰謝才人. The continuous Guangling investiture, Hui’s crown-prince appointment, Jia/Daowen family plot, confinement, Xuchang murder and posthumous Minhuai restoration identify the target. Its own sons are Bin/Zang/Shang. Quoted accusations, forged prayer, personal letter, mourning edicts and historian’s retrospective comments remain distinct attributed frames, not new life events.

sourceAnchor.zh: 甲午，封皇子昱爲琅邪王。

memberAssessments.reason: The 元帝 annal identifies an imperial son 昱 being enfeoffed as Langye prince. This specific 昱 and father’s court differ from 惠帝長子遹, Xizu/Minhuai, who is deposed and killed in the Jia narrative. Neither shared English Yu nor the imperial-son label equates them.

sourceAnchor.zh: 寧康二年七月，簡文帝崩再周而遇閏。

memberAssessments.reason: The funeral-law debate concerns Emperor Jianwen’s second death anniversary under Ningkang, with Xie An, Wang Biaozhi and the later court’s mourning dispute. It is a distinct imperial referent, not the dead crown prince Minhuai in Hui/Jia’s succession narrative. No Western conversion is needed for this source-context distinction.

sourceAnchor.zh: 會稽王昱、中書監庾冰、中書令何充

memberAssessments.reason: The text explicitly distinguishes 會稽王昱 from Yu Bing, He Chong and other officials in the empress-ancestral-sacrifice debate. His specific name 昱, Kuaiji title and later court associates differ from 遹/廣陵王/愍懷太子. The bad English Yu Yi is not proof of another identity or a link to Minhuai.

The complete Teng/Li Feng capture frame lists 虞 among Teng’s four sons; 虞 pursues his father’s killer and is then killed by the remnants. Distinct 虞, parent Teng and his brothers Jiao/Shao/Que distinguish him from Hui’s eldest son 遹 and father of Bin/Zang/Shang. This is affirmative family/event separation, not a guess from Romanization.

This is Emperor Jianwen succeeding at Haixi’s deposition while Huan Wen camps in the central hall and Prince Tian impeaches him. That ruler/event is distinct from Hui’s crown prince Minhuai, whose narrative ends in murder at Xuchang and posthumous restoration as prince.

sourceAnchor.zh: 簡文帝輔政，命為參軍，稱疾不起。

memberAssessments.reason: The Meng Lou biography calls the recruiting regent 簡文帝 and immediately explains Huan Wen’s deference to 會稽王. Specific court status, title and Huan Wen/Meng Lou context distinguish that regent from the Minhuai child/heir in Hui’s household; no borrowed numerical interval is relied on.

sourceAnchor.zh: 二年，騰又遣司馬瑜、周良、石鮮等討之

memberAssessments.reason: The named 瑜 commands with Zhou Liang and Shi Xian against Liu Yuanhai and loses four battles in the Teng military frame. Distinct 瑜 and that command/foe sequence are not the crown prince 遹 imprisoned by Jia. I do not need an inferred office or surname expansion to make this distinction.

sourceAnchor.zh: 廢弈為海西公，立叡子昱。

memberAssessments.reason: The Northern narrative explicitly installs Rui’s son 昱 after Huan Wen deposes Haixi; s0353 makes Changming his successor. The father Rui and son Changming, specific 昱 and ruler succession differ from Hui’s son 遹 and Minhuai’s three sons. The surrounding Tuoba reign frame is the witness’s calendar, not evidence he served Dai.

sourceAnchor.zh: 胤因殺之，並殺允子秦王郁、漢王迪

memberAssessments.reason: The victim 郁 is explicitly Yun’s son and Prince of Qin, killed with his father and brother Di after the Huainan revolt. That family, title and death episode distinguish him from Hui’s son 遹 killed earlier at Xuchang. The corrected s0320 English Yun actor preserves this distinction.

sourceAnchor.zh: 壬辰，冰、充及武陵王晞、會稽王昱、尚書令諸葛恢並受顧命。

memberAssessments.reason: The Kuaiji prince 昱 receives a dying emperor’s commission alongside Yu Bing, He Chong, Wuling Prince Xi and Zhuge Hui in the Cheng/Kang succession frame. Specific 昱, Kuaiji title and this court generation distinguish him from Minhuai 遹; a shared English Yu is insufficient.

sourceAnchor.zh: 帝疾篤，庾冰、庾翼欲立會稽王昱為嗣

memberAssessments.reason: The proposed heir is explicitly 會稽王昱, opposed to installing the emperor’s infant son Dan in the complete court sequence. This different name/title and succession setting distinguish him from Hui’s murdered son 遹. The duplicated English Prince Kuaiji wording is translation debt, not identity uncertainty.

sourceAnchor.zh: 壬戌，以會稽王昱為撫軍大將軍，錄尚書六條事。

memberAssessments.reason: The Kuaiji prince 昱 is appointed to major regency duties and retains Liu Tan, Wang Meng, Han Bo, Xi Chao and Xie Wan around him. That clearly named adult court actor and his title differ from the Hui/Jia crown prince 遹, independently of saved Western-year hints.

sourceAnchor.zh: 謂會稽王昱曰：「溫不可使居形勝之地

memberAssessments.reason: The explicitly named Kuaiji prince 昱 receives Liu Tan’s warning about Huan Wen, declines his proposals and belongs to the later Eastern court. Specific 昱, title and Huan Wen/Liu Tan relation distinguish him from Minhuai 遹 in Hui/Jia’s earlier household.

sourceAnchor.zh: 以左光祿大夫蔡謨領司徒，與會稽王昱同輔政。

memberAssessments.reason: The Kuaiji prince 昱 governs with Cai Mo and writes urging Yin Hao to accept office in s0390f–h. The full named regency/letter frame is not the Minhuai prince’s imprisonment letter to his consort. Specific 昱 and court roles/associates establish separation, without treating the two letters as the same event.

typedOutsideQA.finding: The current idiomatic Yu Yi and literal Prince Hui of Kuaiji Yu garble the explicit Kuaiji Prince 昱. The Chinese owner remains clear; do not interpret that English as an identifying alternative name.
